claim: The EM time series was generated at four classic developmental stages: bean, comma, 1.5-fold and 2-fold stages.
source: We first image an EM time series of C. elegans embryogenesis with data at four classic stages, the bean, comma, 1.5-fold and 2-fold stages (Sulston et al., 1983; Figure 1a).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript text and supported by citation to Sulston et al., 1983.

claim: The EM series spans a critical 150-min time window during embryogenesis.
source: The EM series spans a critical 150-min time window during which most tissues undergo major morphological changes: pharyngeal and intestinal lumens develop, distinctive morphologies develop in muscles and the excretory system, the epidermis spreads and closes over the embryo, and the body length doubles.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript text describing the temporal extent of the EM series.

claim: The bean and comma stage embryos were imaged with Focused Ion Beam-Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM).
source: As part of the effort to test and demonstrate the feasibility of EM time series acquisition, the bean and comma stage embryos are imaged with Focused Ion Beam-Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM) while the 1.5- and 2-fold stage embryos are imaged with Array Tomography (AT).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript describing the imaging methods used for different stages.

claim: The 1.5- and 2-fold stage embryos were imaged with Array Tomography (AT).
source: As part of the effort to test and demonstrate the feasibility of EM time series acquisition, the bean and comma stage embryos are imaged with Focused Ion Beam-Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM) while the 1.5- and 2-fold stage embryos are imaged with Array Tomography (AT).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript describing the imaging methods used for different stages.

claim: The lateral resolution of the EM images ranges from 8.5 to 19.4 nm.
source: The lateral resolution ranges from 8.5 to 19.4 nm, and z spacing 25–85 nm (see Supplementary file 1a and Methods).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with reference to supplementary data.

claim: The z spacing of the EM images ranges from 25–85 nm.
source: The lateral resolution ranges from 8.5 to 19.4 nm, and z spacing 25–85 nm (see Supplementary file 1a and Methods).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with reference to supplementary data.

claim: Entire embryos were imaged, containing 576–601 cells including visible apoptotic cells.
source: Entire embryos were imaged, containing 576–601 cells including visible apoptotic cells (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with reference to supplementary data.

claim: The FM series typically begin at the four-cell stage and continue for approximately 8 hr until the 1.75-fold stage.
source: These image series typically begin at the four-cell stage and continue for approximately 8 hr until the 1.75-fold stage and the onset of embryonic movement, with a temporal resolution of 60 or 75 s.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript describing the FM imaging protocol.

claim: The FM series have a temporal resolution of 60 or 75 s.
source: These image series typically begin at the four-cell stage and continue for approximately 8 hr until the 1.75-fold stage and the onset of embryonic movement, with a temporal resolution of 60 or 75 s.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript describing the FM imaging protocol.

claim: The nuclear labels are used to trace the entire cell lineage and provide the position and lineage identity of every cell at every time point.
source: The nuclear labels are used to trace the entire cell lineage and provide the position and lineage identity of every cell at every time point (Santella et al., 2014; Katzman et al., 2018) (see Figure 3—video 1).

claim: The aligned EM data are timed as approximately 320, 345, and 380 min post first cell division (pfc).
source: Based on the timing of known developmental events in the FM series, the aligned EM data are timed as approximately 320, 345, and 380 min post first cell division (pfc), see Materials and methods for details.

claim: During the developmental window examined, 75 cell divisions and 76 deaths occur.

claim: The ensemble FM model for each EM dataset contains 39 labeled 3D FM images of embryos.

claim: In cross-modality applications there is generally little shared appearance.
source: However, in cross-modality applications there is generally little shared appearance.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript as a challenge in cross-modality alignment.

claim: Performance of landmark-based alignment methods is limited with dense landmarks (typically 50–60% accuracy, at best).
source: To account for complex variation of landmark positions (Toyoshima et al., 2020; Insley and Shaham, 2018), a variety of approaches are used to exploit relative position to improve matching accuracy (Lalit et al., 2020; Yu, 2021; Long et al., 2009; Chaudhary et al., 2021; Preibisch et al., 2010), but performance is limited with dense landmarks (typically 50–60% accuracy, at best).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with supporting citations.

claim: Multi-color labeling to distinguish landmarks can greatly improve matching performance (to 81–86%).
source: Efforts to build in additional information such as multi-color labeling to distinguish the landmarks, while technically difficult, can greatly improve matching performance (to 81–86%) (Yemini et al., 2021; Chaudhary et al., 2021).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with supporting citations.

claim: Different developmental processes show slight variation of developmental speed, creating heterochrony among anatomical structures.
source: Different developmental processes show slight variation of developmental speed, creating heterochrony among anatomical structures.

claim: Between samples of comparable developmental stage, certain cell types and tissues/organs may or may not be present, causing a mismatch in the landmarks present.

evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript as a challenge in developmental data alignment.

source: Alignment using manually selected landmarks that are always present across samples partially bypasses these challenges (Wong et al., 2015).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with supporting citation.

claim: Efforts at alignment that largely ignore heterochrony discrepancies between individuals have limited accuracy (<50%).
source: Efforts at alignment that largely ignore these discrepancies between individuals have also been attempted, with limited accuracy (<50%) (Lalit et al., 2020).
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with supporting citation.

claim: EM studies in C. elegans have made profound contributions to neuroscience including the first connectome.

evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with supporting citations.

claim: The ensemble model contains three parts: the set of labeled data; a neighbor graph representing consistent estimated adjacencies; and the set of variable landmarks.
source: The ensemble model contains three parts (Figure 2a) in order to capture the regularity and developmental variations of the anatomy: the set of labeled data; a neighbor graph representing consistent estimated adjacencies (see Materials and methods) observed between landmarks across individual labeled datasets; and the set of variable landmarks whose presence is inconsistent among labeled data.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript with figure reference.

claim: The consistent adjacencies graph captures relative positions, which makes it insensitive to body size variation, or shifting between organs and tissues.
source: The adjacency graph captures relative positions, which makes it insensitive to body size variation, or shifting between organs and tissues due to posture, sample distortion or heterochrony in development, since the invariant positional relationships within a given organ/tissue are preserved in the graph.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript as a property of the approach.

source: The approach is further motivated by biology. Physical adhesion between cells and tissues underlie anatomical regularity.

source: Consistent adjacencies over multiple samples enrich for the bona fide regularity caused by some underlying physical driver and removes coincidental adjacencies.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript as reasoning for the approach.

claim: Inconsistent landmarks are likely discrepancies, which can be used to deliberately modify a labeled dataset to reduce discrepancies and improve alignment success.

source: Ablating all of the unique components of our approach leaves the prior method of an LAP matching based on distance (after pre-alignment) to each labeled example followed by voting, this has accuracy of 43–66%.
evidence: Directly stated in the manuscript describing ablation study results.
